_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Kazakhstan covering Scythian/Saka nomads, Turkic khaganates, Silk Road cities, Mongol conquest, Kazakh Khanate (1465), Zhuz (horde) system, Russian colonisation, Soviet era (Virgin Lands, nuclear testing at Semipalatinsk), December 1986 protests, independence 1991, Nazarbayev era, capital move to Astana, oil-driven economy, and Tokayev reforms.

religion.note: Secular state; Islam among Kazakhs is traditionally moderate/nomadic-influenced; Congress of Leaders of World Religions hosted in Astana

ethnic_groups.name: Kazakh
ethnic_groups.notes: Turkic; three zhuz (hordes): Great (south), Middle (central/east), Little (west); nomadic pastoralist heritage; eagle hunting; yurt culture; percentage rising due to oralman (ethnic Kazakh returnee) policy

ethnic_groups.name: Russian
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern/eastern Kazakhstan; declining (was 37% at independence); Slavic; Orthodox; many emigrating; Cossack communities; Russian-language dominance in cities

ethnic_groups.name: Uzbek
ethnic_groups.notes: Turkestan/Shymkent; Turkic; cross-border with Uzbekistan; farming

ethnic_groups.name: Ukrainian
ethnic_groups.notes: Soviet-era settlers; northern oblasts; declining; farming

ethnic_groups.name: Uyghur
ethnic_groups.notes: Almaty region; Turkic; cross-border with Xinjiang, China; some separatist sentiment concerns

ethnic_groups.name: German
ethnic_groups.notes: Deported from Volga 1941; was 6% at independence; most repatriated to Germany (Aussiedler); Karaganda area

ethnic_groups.name: Korean (Koryo-saram)
ethnic_groups.notes: Deported from Soviet Far East 1937 by Stalin; ~100,000; well-integrated; farming/business

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Dungan, Chechen, Kurdish, Polish, Belarusian)
ethnic_groups.notes: Diverse Soviet deportee communities; Dungan (Chinese Hui Muslims); Meskhetian Turks; total 130+ ethnicities; 'laboratory of inter-ethnic harmony' (official narrative)

independence.from: Soviet Union (last republic to declare independence)

country_profile.notes_unique: World's largest landlocked country (9th overall); Baikonur Cosmodrome (leased to Russia); Tengiz/Kashagan oil fields; former Soviet nuclear test site (Semipalatinsk, 456 tests); voluntarily gave up nuclear weapons; apple originated here (alma = apple, Almaty = city of apples)

current_leader.name: Kassym-Jomart Tokayev
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Amanat party; career diplomat; succeeded Nazarbayev; January 2022 unrest (Bloody January); broke with Nazarbayev; 'New Kazakhstan' reforms; CSTO called in Russian troops

former_presidents.name: Nursultan Nazarbayev
former_presidents.notes: First president; 'Elbasy' (Leader of the Nation); 29-year rule; moved capital to Astana (renamed Nur-Sultan 2019-2022, reverted to Astana); oil wealth; authoritarian; personality cult; stripped of powers after January 2022 unrest

910.name: Ancient Steppe Cultures
910.description: The earliest civilizations of the Kazakh steppe, from the Botai culture's pioneering horse domestication to the Saka and Scythian nomadic confederations and their spectacular gold art.

sub_clusters.name: Botai Culture and Horse Domestication
sub_clusters.description: The Botai settlement in northern Kazakhstan, one of the earliest known sites of horse domestication, transforming steppe life and ultimately world history.
key_events: Botai people domesticate horses on the northern Kazakh steppe (c. 3500 BC)
Evidence of mare's milk consumption — earliest known kumis production

sub_clusters.name: Saka and Scythian Nomads
sub_clusters.description: The Saka confederations of the Kazakh steppe, their elaborate animal-style gold art, the 'Golden Man' of Issyk, and conflicts with the Achaemenid Persian Empire.
key_events: The 'Golden Man' burial at Issyk kurgan, iconic symbol of Kazakh heritage (c. 4th–3rd century BC)

910.name: Hunnic and Early Turkic Period
910.description: The Xiongnu and Hunnic movements across the Kazakh steppe, the rise of the First and Second Turkic Khaganates, and the establishment of Turkic linguistic and cultural dominance in the region.

sub_clusters.name: Xiongnu and Hunnic Migrations
sub_clusters.description: The Xiongnu confederacy's influence on the Kazakh steppe, the Kangju state, and the westward migrations of Hunnic peoples reshaping Central Asian demographics.

sub_clusters.name: Göktürk Khaganates
sub_clusters.description: The First and Second Turkic Khaganates spanning from Mongolia to the Kazakh steppe, the creation of the Old Turkic script, and the establishment of a Turkic political and cultural framework.
key_events: Bumin Qaghan founds the First Turkic Khaganate, unifying the steppe (552 AD)
Orkhon inscriptions — earliest known Turkic written monuments (c. 735 AD)

910.name: Karluk and Karakhanid States
910.description: The Karluk and Oghuz Turkic states on the Kazakh steppe, the Islamization of the Turkic peoples under the Karakhanids, and the great scholar Al-Farabi.

sub_clusters.name: Karluk, Oghuz, and Kimek Confederations
sub_clusters.description: The Karluk successor state to the Göktürks, the Oghuz Yabgu State in western Kazakhstan, and the Kimek-Kipchak confederacy dominating the northern steppe.

sub_clusters.name: Karakhanid Dynasty and Islamization
sub_clusters.description: The Karakhanid conversion to Islam — the first Turkic Muslim dynasty — Mahmud Kashgari's Turkic dictionary, Yusuf Balasaguni's Kutadgu Bilig, and the flowering of Turkic-Islamic civilization.
key_events: Sultan Satuq Bughra Khan converts to Islam, founding the Karakhanid dynasty (c. 960 AD)
Mahmud Kashgari compiles the Diwan Lughat al-Turk, first Turkic dictionary (1072–1074)

920.name: Mongol Conquest and Golden Horde
920.description: The devastating Mongol conquest of the Kazakh steppe under Genghis Khan, the region's incorporation into the Chagatai Khanate and Golden Horde, and the political fragmentation following Timur's campaigns.

sub_clusters.name: Genghis Khan and Mongol Devastation
sub_clusters.description: Genghis Khan's conquest of the Khwarazmian Empire, the destruction of Otrar and other Central Asian cities, and the division of the Kazakh lands between the Chagatai and Jochi uluses.
key_events: Mongol forces destroy Otrar after the massacre of Genghis Khan's trade envoys (1219–1220)
Kazakh steppe divided between the Golden Horde (Jochi ulus) and Chagatai Khanate

sub_clusters.name: White Horde and Post-Mongol Fragmentation
sub_clusters.description: The White Horde in eastern Dasht-i Kipchak, Timur's devastating campaigns through the region, the decline of the Golden Horde, and the emergence of the Uzbek Khanate under Abu'l-Khayr.

920.name: Kazakh Khanate
920.description: The founding and evolution of the Kazakh Khanate as the first distinctly Kazakh state, the three jüz (hordes) system, the struggle against the Dzungar Mongols, and the gradual Russian encroachment.

sub_clusters.name: Foundation and Golden Age
sub_clusters.description: Janibek and Kerey's founding of the Kazakh Khanate by breaking from Abu'l-Khayr's Uzbek confederation, the consolidation under Kasym Khan, and the khanate's territorial expansion.
key_events: Janibek and Kerey lead Kazakh tribes away from Abu'l-Khayr, founding the Kazakh Khanate (1465)
Kasym Khan expands the khanate to over one million subjects — the 'Gatherer of the Kazakh Lands' (c. 1511)

sub_clusters.name: Three Jüz System and Dzungar Wars
sub_clusters.description: The emergence of the Great, Middle, and Little Jüz (hordes), the catastrophic Dzungar invasions known as the 'Great Disaster' (Aqtaban Shubyryndy), and the heroic resistance of Kazakh batyrs.
key_events: The 'Great Disaster' (Aqtaban Shubyryndy) — Dzungar invasions devastate the Kazakhs (1723–1727)
Battle of Anyrakay — decisive Kazakh victory over the Dzungars (1730)

sub_clusters.name: Russian Protectorate and Khanate Decline
sub_clusters.description: The Little Jüz's acceptance of Russian protection under Abul Khair Khan, the gradual Russian absorption of the three jüz, and the abolition of the khanate system.
key_events: Abul Khair Khan of the Little Jüz accepts Russian protectorate status (1731)

930.name: Silk Road Cities and Trade
930.description: The great Silk Road trading cities on Kazakh territory — Otrar, Taraz, Turkestan — their role as crossroads of civilizations, and the cultural and economic exchange between East and West.

sub_clusters.name: Silk Road Urban Centers
sub_clusters.description: The development of cities like Otrar, Taraz, Sauran, and Turkestan as major stops on the Silk Road, blending Sogdian, Turkic, Persian, and Chinese cultural influences.

sub_clusters.name: Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi
sub_clusters.description: The life and legacy of Sufi mystic Khoja Ahmed Yasawi, founder of the Yasawiyya order, and Timur's construction of the magnificent unfinished mausoleum in Turkestan.
key_events: Timur commissions the grand mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi in Turkestan (1389–1405)

940.name: Russian Colonial Period
940.description: The full incorporation of Kazakhstan into the Russian Empire, the construction of military fortification lines, the settlement of Russian and Ukrainian peasants, and Kazakh uprisings against colonial rule.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Conquest and Resistance
sub_clusters.description: The abolition of the Kazakh khanate, the establishment of Russian military and administrative control, Kenesary Khan's resistance war, and the disruption of nomadic pastoral life.
key_events: Kenesary Khan leads the last major Kazakh uprising against Russian rule (1837–1847)

sub_clusters.name: Settler Colonialism and 1916 Revolt
sub_clusters.description: The Stolypin reforms bringing millions of Slavic settlers to Kazakh lands, the forced sedentarization of nomads, and the 1916 Central Asian Revolt against wartime conscription.
key_events: 1916 Central Asian Revolt — Kazakhs resist conscription into Russian labor battalions
Brutal Russian suppression kills tens of thousands and displaces hundreds of thousands of Kazakhs

950.name: Soviet Kazakhstan
950.description: Kazakhstan's transformation under Soviet rule: the horrific collectivization famine, the industrialization and Virgin Lands campaign, the gulag system, nuclear testing at Semipalatinsk, and the December 1986 protests.

sub_clusters.name: Revolution and Collectivization Famine
sub_clusters.description: The Russian Revolution's impact, the Alash Orda autonomy movement, and the devastating collectivization famine (Asharshylyk) of 1931–1933 that killed an estimated 1.5 million Kazakhs — roughly 40% of the population.
key_events: Alash Orda declares Kazakh autonomy during the Russian Civil War (1917–1920)
Collectivization famine (Asharshylyk) kills approximately 1.5 million Kazakhs (1931–1933)

sub_clusters.name: Industrialization and Nuclear Testing
sub_clusters.description: Forced industrialization, the deportation of entire peoples (Koreans, Chechens, Germans) to Kazakhstan, the Virgin Lands campaign, the Baikonur Cosmodrome, and the devastating nuclear testing program at Semipalatinsk.
key_events: First Soviet nuclear test at Semipalatinsk — beginning of 456 nuclear detonations (1949)
Yuri Gagarin launches into space from Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan (1961)

sub_clusters.name: Jeltoqsan and Late Soviet Period
sub_clusters.description: Dinmukhamed Kunayev's long rule, the December 1986 Jeltoqsan protests against Moscow's appointment of an ethnic Russian leader, and the Nevada-Semipalatinsk anti-nuclear movement.
key_events: Jeltoqsan protests in Alma-Ata — first major anti-Soviet nationalist demonstration (December 1986)
Nevada-Semipalatinsk movement leads to closure of the nuclear test site (1989–1991)

960.name: Independent Kazakhstan
960.description: Kazakhstan's emergence as the largest Central Asian state: Nursultan Nazarbayev's authoritarian modernization, nuclear disarmament, oil-driven economic boom, the new capital Astana, and the 2022 political transition.

sub_clusters.name: Nazarbayev Era and Nation-Building
sub_clusters.description: Nursultan Nazarbayev's three-decade presidency, voluntary nuclear disarmament, the move of the capital from Almaty to Astana, massive oil and mineral wealth development, and authoritarian stability.
key_events: Kazakhstan voluntarily relinquishes the world's fourth-largest nuclear arsenal (1993–1995)
Capital officially moved from Almaty to Astana (1997)

sub_clusters.name: Tokayev Transition and Bloody January
sub_clusters.description: The transfer of power to Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, the January 2022 mass protests (Qandy Qantar / Bloody January), CSTO intervention, and Tokayev's political reforms distancing from the Nazarbayev legacy.
key_events: Nazarbayev resigns the presidency; Tokayev succeeds him (March 2019)
Bloody January (Qandy Qantar) — mass protests and violent crackdown kill over 200 (January 2022)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
